topic.title: Configure the AI Service Using a JSON File

body.p: The Oxygen AI Positron add-on can automatically configure its AI service by using a JSON file placed in the plugin's installation directory. This method initializes the connector when Oxygen starts and hides the AI Service Configuration preferences page. As a result, users can use only the company's approved AI service.

section.title: Configuration File Example
section.p:
Create a file named ai-service-configuration.json. You can place the file in one of the following locations:
Inside an ai-positron-actions folder in any framework installed in the application.
Inside an ai-positron-actions folder in any plugin installed in the application.
Directly inside the AI Positron plugin's installation directory. In the Preferences Plugins page, you can select the AI Positron plugin. The Location field points to the plugin's installation folder. This is the exact location where you must copy the JSON file.

The supported connectors are open-ai-connector, open-ai-responses-api-connector, ms-azure-open-ai-connector, claude-ai-connector, google-gemini-ai-connector, aws-bedrock-connector, grok-connector, and vertex-ai-service. The latter is only available when the separate Oxygen AI Positron Vertex AI Connector add-on is also installed.
The configuration file accepts either a single JSON object (for one connection) or a JSON array of objects (for multiple connections).
Examples of single connections:
The organization_param parameter sets the OpenAI organization ID to which requests are billed and scoped.
The enable_text_moderation_param and enable_speech_to_text_param parameters (both true by default) toggle OpenAI's moderation endpoint and Whisper speech-to-text integration.

The extra_headers_param parameter (also supported by open-ai-responses-api-connector, ms-azure-open-ai-connector, claude-ai-connector, and aws-bedrock-connector) adds custom HTTP headers to every request sent through the connector. Its value is an array of {"first": "<header-name>", "second": "<header-value>"} objects.

The reasoning_effort_param parameter sets the default reasoning effort (low, medium, or high) applied when actions and chat requests run on that deployment. Individual actions can still override it. To use the deployment's built-in default effort, omit the parameter or leave it empty.

The max_context_window_param parameter declares the deployment's context window size in tokens. It is used by the chat context usage indicator, because it cannot be derived automatically from an open-ended Azure deployment name.

The ms_azure_speech_region and ms_azure_speech_subscription_key parameters configure the Azure Speech service used for speech-to-text in the chat panel. Both are optional, and the key (e.g. ai_key_param) is supplied through its own _encrypted_url/_seed_url pair.

The max_context_window_param parameter declares the model's context window size in tokens, since it cannot be derived automatically from an arbitrary Bedrock model ID. It is used by the chat context usage indicator.

By default, or when aws_bedrock_auth_type_param is omitted or set to api_key, authentication uses aws_bedrock_api_key_param, as shown above. Set aws_bedrock_auth_type_param to aws_credentials to authenticate with a local AWS profile/SSO session instead (desktop add-on only):
The aws_bedrock_profile_param parameter is optional. When it is set and aws_bedrock_auth_refresh_cmd_param is left empty, the refresh command defaults to aws sso login --profile=<profile>.

The open-ai-responses-api-connector accepts the same connector_params as open-ai-connector (only its connector_id differs), since it is the same OpenAI backend accessed through the Responses API instead of the Chat Completions API.

Vertex AI has no fixed model catalog, so its models_table_param starts with only a single default model. Any other model must be added as a custom entry in userModels, as shown above. If credentials_param is omitted, the connector falls back to Google Cloud's Application Default Credentials.

section.title: Configuring Models
section.p:
The ms-azure-open-ai-connector and aws-bedrock-connector take the model as a plain text value (deployment_param and model_param, respectively), as shown in the examples above. All other connectors (open-ai-connector, open-ai-responses-api-connector, claude-ai-connector, google-gemini-ai-connector, grok-connector, and vertex-ai-service) manage models through an admin-curated models table instead, exposed as the models_table_param parameter. Its value is a JSON object, not a plain string, and every field in it is optional:
defaultModelId - The ID of the model that becomes the connection's selected/default model. It must match one of the connector's built-in model IDs or the ID of a model added through userModels (see below). Matching is case-insensitive. If models_table_param is omitted entirely, or if defaultModelId does not match any known model ID, the connector falls back to its own built-in default model without raising an error.
userModels - An array used to add models that are not in the connector's built-in list or to override a built-in model's display name or reasoning settings. Each entry needs a unique id. For a brand-new model, isCustom must also be set to true. Otherwise, the entry is silently discarded. Other optional fields on an entry are displayName, reasoningLevel (one of off, auto, none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, or max), requestModelId (the model ID actually sent to the AI provider when it differs from id), visibleInUI, and the token limits maxTotalTokens, maxInputTokens, and maxOutputTokens.
removedDefaultIds - An array of built-in model IDs to hide from users.

section.title: Configuring Multiple Connections
section.p: To expose more than one AI connection to users, provide a JSON array instead of a single object. Each entry follows the same structure as a single-connection file. When multiple connections are defined, the first one in the array becomes the active connection. section.title: Configuration File Detection
section.p: When the configuration file is detected, the connector is initialized with its values when Oxygen starts. The Plugins Oxygen AI Positron AI Service Configuration preferences page is then hidden. After setup, you can remove the encrypted key and seed endpoints if they are no longer needed. Any changes to the configuration file are applied after you restart Oxygen.

section.title: How to Obtain the Encrypted Key
section.p: Install the Oxygen AI Positron API Key Encryption add-on to generate the encrypted API key. To install this add-on, follow these steps:

ol.li: Go to Help Install new add-ons to open the add-on selection dialog box. Enter or paste https://www.oxygenxml.com/InstData/Addons/optional/updateSite.xml in the Show add-ons from field, or select it from the drop-down menu.
Select the Oxygen AI Positron API Key Encryption add-on and click Next.

section.p:
To obtain the encrypted API key:
Open the API Key Tools: From the main menu, select API Key Tools.
Select the Encrypt Action: Choose Encrypt... from the API Key Tools menu.
Enter Your API Key: Follow the prompts to enter your encryption key and API key. The tool encrypts the API key by using the encryption key.
Publish the encryption key and the encrypted API key: Publish the encryption key and the encrypted API key to the URLs referenced in the configuration file.
